title: smoke_ConvertCPULayerTest_7D_Dynamic fails on CPU primitive type check (unknown_f32 vs ref_f32)

root_cause: The test asserts that the executed CPU graph node reports a specific implementation type (selectedType == ref_f32) via the IMPL_TYPE execution-graph property, checked in CPUTestsBase::primTypeCheck (cpu_test_utils.cpp:248). The observed node reported 'unknown_f32' instead, meaning the convert node's selected/queried implementation metadata did not match what the test expects for this particular dynamic 7D shape range (large bounded dynamic dims 1..5/2..22/2..9 with multiple 1..4 ranges) and f32->i8 conversion. This mismatch happens for a single parameterized case out of 71641 executed smoke tests (59793 passed), strongly suggesting either (a) a transient/order-dependent primitive selection issue for this specific shape combination rather than a systemic regression introduced by the merged PR (#38463, a GPU-only SDPA fix unrelated to CPU Convert nodes), or (b) a latent flakiness in how the CPU plugin reports IMPL_TYPE for dynamic-shape Convert kernels with this dimension pattern. The merged PR only touches the GPU plugin's SDPA opt implementation, so it is very unlikely to be the direct cause of a CPU plugin primitive-type mismatch; this looks environment/shape-dependent rather than a code regression from this commit.
reproduction_steps:
Build the CPU functional test binary and run the specific test:

OV_CPU_DEBUG_LOG=1 ./bin/intel64/Release/ov_cpu_func_tests --gtest_filter='smoke_ConvertCPULayerTest_7D_Dynamic/ConvertCPULayerTest.CompareWithRefs/IS=*1..5.2..22.2..9.1..4.1..4.1..4.1..4*inputPRC=f32_specialValue=none_targetPRC=i8_*'

If it does not reproduce on the first run, repeat several times (test_parallel_runner ran this suite with 71641 tests and only this one case failed, suggesting shape- or scheduling-order sensitivity).
recommended_actions: Re-run the single failing test case (`smoke_ConvertCPULayerTest_7D_Dynamic/ConvertCPULayerTest.CompareWithRefs` with the given IS/TS parameters) in isolation and in a full-suite run to confirm whether it is flaky or deterministically reproducible.

If deterministic, inspect the CPU Convert node's primitive descriptor selection logic for this specific dynamic shape range (bounded dims 1..5, 2..22, 2..9) to see why IMPL_TYPE resolves to 'unknown_f32' instead of 'ref_f32' for f32->i8 conversion.
Check whether the PR #38463 GPU SDPA change or an unrelated concurrent merge affected shared CPU plugin build artifacts/caches used by this CI run.
If confirmed flaky, consider adding this parameterized case to the disabled/known-flaky test list with a tracking ticket, or add a retry wrapper for it pending root-cause fix.
prevention_strategies: Add stability tracking for individual parameterized CPU functional test cases that intermittently fail on primType/IMPL_TYPE assertions, and periodically audit implementation-type selection paths for Convert nodes handling large bounded-dynamic multi-dimensional shapes to rule out dynamic-shape-dependent kernel dispatch edge cases.
historical_context: A related but distinct pattern (signature_hash d94563b07437b23b) was previously recorded on 2026-09-30: smoke_AvgPool_CPU_4D failing on an ACL primitive type check (undef_f32 vs acl_f32), also a single-test primType mismatch in the same cpu_test_utils.cpp assertion but for a different test suite (ACL AvgPool) and different expected/actual values. This indicates primType/IMPL_TYPE assertion flakiness in CPU functional tests has occurred more than once across different kernels (ACL pooling, now plain CPU Convert), suggesting a broader intermittent issue in how exec-graph IMPL_TYPE is reported rather than an isolated one-off.
